issues.description: The attribute 'numberOfTutors' is specified as type int in the problem statement UML (problem_statement.md line 68), but in the solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) the backing field is declared as short and the API uses short for constructor and setter parameters. Specifically: problem_statement.md declares '-numberOfTutors: int' (line 68); solution file defines 'private short numberOfTutors;' (Lecture.java line 10), the constructor parameter 'short numberOfTutors' (Lecture.java line 13) and the setter 'public void setNumberOfTutors(short numberOfTutors)' (Lecture.java line 58). This type mismatch between the specification (int) and the solution's field and parameter types will confuse students and can cause compilation or usage problems because int values/literals cannot be passed to the constructor or setter without an explicit cast.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the UML/specification by using int for the tutors attribute and related API. Change the field to 'private int numberOfTutors;', update the constructor parameter to 'int numberOfTutors', and change the setter to 'public void setNumberOfTutors(int numberOfTutors)'. Also ensure any uses of the field/parameter types in the class are updated accordingly so the implementation matches the exercise specification.
